Shared predictive importance with fold-internal residualization (UMFI-LR)

Source: R/shared_importance.R
shared_importance.Rd

For every anchor feature, shared_importance() residualizes the other predictors on the anchor using ordinary least squares coefficients estimated on the training rows of each resampling split, applies the same coefficients to the assessment rows, fits the learner to the full representation (anchor plus residualized others) and to the reduced representation (residualized others only), and compares their assessment-set performance. This is the linear-regression variant of ultra-marginal feature importance (UMFI-LR) of Janssen, Guan and Robeva (2023), evaluated out of sample with paired splits. The R and Python packages follow one common specification (docs/specification.md in the source repository).

Usage

shared_importance(
  x,
  y,
  learner = "rand_forest",
  metric = NULL,
  task = c("auto", "regression", "classification"),
  v = 5,
  repeats = 1,
  resamples = NULL,
  features = NULL,
  seed = NULL,
  on_error = c("warn", "error"),
  verbose = FALSE
)

Arguments

x

A numeric matrix or a data frame whose columns are all numeric. Missing values are not allowed. A single column is allowed; the reduced model is then the null model (training mean or class frequencies).

y

The response: a numeric vector for regression or a factor for classification (binary or multiclass; the first level is the event level for probability metrics). Character vectors are converted to factors.

learner

"rand_forest" (default), "linear", a parsnip model specification, or a sharedimp_learner(). Hyperparameters are fixed; no tuning is performed. See sharedimp_learner() for details.

metric

A built-in metric name or a yardstick metric function. The defaults are "mse" for regression and "log_loss" for classification. See as_metric().

task

"auto" (default: numeric y is regression, factor y is classification), "regression", or "classification".

v, repeats

Number of folds and repeats for rsample::vfold_cv(), used when resamples is NULL. Classification folds are stratified by y.

resamples

Optional explicit resampling: an rsample rset built on data with nrow(x) rows, or an integer vector of length nrow(x) whose unique values label the assessment fold of each row. Overrides v and repeats. Explicit splits are the mechanism for comparisons with the Python implementation.

features

Optional names or indices of the anchor features to evaluate. Default: all columns of x.

seed

Optional integer. When supplied, fold generation and any stochastic learner run under a local RNG state seeded with seed, and the caller's RNG state is restored afterwards.

on_error

"warn" (default) records a learner failure on a split as NA, aggregates over the remaining splits and warns; "error" stops at the first failure.

verbose

Print progress messages?

Value

An object of class sharedimp_result (see sharedimp_result) with elements importance (tibble with the common columns feature, importance, importance_std, score_full, score_reduced, n_splits), folds (per-split paired scores; see fold_results()), metric, task, learner, and bookkeeping fields n, p, v, repeats, seed, levels, resampling, call.

Scores and sign convention

Every metric is reported as a score oriented so that greater is better: the metric value itself for a metric to maximize ("r2", "accuracy", "roc_auc", ...), and its negative for a metric to minimize ("mse", "rmse", "mae", "log_loss", ...). For each split, importance = score_full - score_reduced, so a positive value always means that keeping the anchor predicts better than the residualized others alone. Negative values are reported as they are; they are never truncated to zero. The reported importance is the mean over splits; importance_std is the sample standard deviation of the split values and is a descriptive quantity only, not a standard error.

What the numbers are not

The values are out-of-sample predictive gains for a particular learner, metric and resampling scheme. They are not causal effects, not regression coefficients and not conditional effects, and the package deliberately provides no confidence intervals or p-values.

References

Janssen, J., Guan, V. and Robeva, E. (2023). Ultra-marginal Feature Importance: Learning from Data with Causal Guarantees. AISTATS 2023, PMLR 206:10782-10814. https://proceedings.mlr.press/v206/janssen23a.html

Examples

set.seed(1)
n <- 150
x <- data.frame(x1 = rnorm(n), x2 = rnorm(n), x3 = rnorm(n))
x$x4 <- x$x1 + rnorm(n, sd = 0.1) # near duplicate of x1
y <- 2 * x$x1 + x$x2 + rnorm(n)

# Fast, deterministic linear learner with the MSE metric
res <- shared_importance(x, y, learner = "linear", v = 5, seed = 1)
res
#> <sharedimp_result>
#>   task:       regression
#>   learner:    linear
#>   metric:     mse (minimize); score = -mse, importance = score_full - score_reduced
#>   resampling: 5-fold cross-validation (1 repeat)
#> 
#> # A tibble: 4 × 6
#>   feature importance importance_std score_full score_reduced n_splits
#>   <chr>        <dbl>          <dbl>      <dbl>         <dbl>    <int>
#> 1 x1         3.18            0.809       -1.33         -4.51        5
#> 2 x2         0.920           0.383       -1.33         -2.25        5
#> 3 x3         0.00634         0.0250      -1.33         -1.34        5
#> 4 x4         3.13            0.865       -1.33         -4.46        5
fold_results(res)
#> # A tibble: 20 × 10
#>    feature split n_train n_test score_full score_reduced importance id    id2  
#>    <chr>   <int>   <int>  <int>      <dbl>         <dbl>      <dbl> <chr> <chr>
#>  1 x1          1     120     30      -1.02         -4.31    3.29    Fold1 NA   
#>  2 x2          1     120     30      -1.02         -2.22    1.20    Fold1 NA   
#>  3 x3          1     120     30      -1.02         -1.03    0.00905 Fold1 NA   
#>  4 x4          1     120     30      -1.02         -4.49    3.47    Fold1 NA   
#>  5 x1          2     120     30      -1.85         -4.00    2.15    Fold2 NA   
#>  6 x2          2     120     30      -1.85         -2.53    0.688   Fold2 NA   
#>  7 x3          2     120     30      -1.85         -1.89    0.0398  Fold2 NA   
#>  8 x4          2     120     30      -1.85         -3.69    1.85    Fold2 NA   
#>  9 x1          3     120     30      -1.25         -3.92    2.67    Fold3 NA   
#> 10 x2          3     120     30      -1.25         -1.61    0.364   Fold3 NA   
#> 11 x3          3     120     30      -1.25         -1.24   -0.00375 Fold3 NA   
#> 12 x4          3     120     30      -1.25         -3.92    2.67    Fold3 NA

# Binary classification with accuracy
yb <- factor(ifelse(y > median(y), "high", "low"))
shared_importance(x, yb, learner = "linear", metric = "accuracy", v = 5, seed = 1)
#> <sharedimp_result>
#>   task:       classification (2 classes)
#>   learner:    linear
#>   metric:     accuracy (maximize); score = accuracy, importance = score_full - score_reduced

shared_importance(x, y, v = 5, seed = 1)
